extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, statesmen, and readers of political philosophy (rulers and students of governance)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance for sovereigns on maintaining the stability and welfare of a commonwealth: diagnosis of political 'diseases', the sovereign's obligations (laws, instruction, justice, taxation, punishments, rewards), and criteria for good governance and advisers. Drawn from a political treatise addressing how a sovereign should secure peace and public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dual civil and spiritual supremacy
rubrics_metrics.description: When both Civil and Ghostly (spiritual) Power each claim to declare what is Law, the people must obey two masters and the commonwealth is in danger of civil war and dissolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either the Civil must be subordinate to the Ghostly or vice versa; if both oppose each other the state risks large-scale conflict. Because civil authority is more visible it draws people, but spiritual terrors also attract a sufficient party to trouble or destroy the commonwealth; analogous to a possession causing convulsions in a body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent mixed government producing multiple sovereigns
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'mixed' government in which different essential powers (levying money, conduct/command, making laws) depend on different independent bodies effectively divides the commonwealth into independent factions rather than one representative person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such division endangers provision (nourishment) and consent for laws. Multiple bodies bearing 'the person of the people' produce three sovereigns, not one, and thus cannot maintain unity or proper government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure capacity to raise money for public needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign must be able to raise money for necessary uses (especially approaching war); obstruction by subjects' sense of property threatens the state's survival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sovereign cannot obtain funds by legal measures he may be forced to use violence; repeated extremities either break the people's contumacy or lead to the commonwealth's ruin. Hobbes compares this instability to the ague: initial contraction then violent effort to restore flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent monopolies and abuses of public revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentration of the commonwealth's treasure in a few private hands (by monopolies or farms of public revenues) damages the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such accumulation is likened to pleurisy where blood gathers and causes inflammation—i.e., it breeds political inflammation and disease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control popular and ambitious subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The popularity of an ambitious subject can be a dangerous disease, as flattery and reputation draw people away from obedience to the laws toward following a man whose virtues or designs are unknown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This often manifests as rebellion (e.g., Julius Caesar). The phenomenon resembles witchcraft for its power to dazzle and mislead the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against excessive urban power and corporate factionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: An immoderately large town able to furnish a great army, or too many corporations (like lesser commonwealths within), is an infirmity of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These internal centers of power act like worms in the entrails, undermining unity and enabling internal division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress liberty of disputing against absolute sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom to dispute sovereign authority, propagated by pretenders to political prudence and false doctrines, perpetually meddles with fundamental laws and molests the commonwealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disputation is compared to intestinal worms (ascarides) that disturb the body; doctrines denying sovereign rights must be countered because they seed disobedience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insatiable appetite to enlarge dominion and ununited conquests
rubrics_metrics.description: An ever-growing desire to enlarge dominion (bulimia) and keeping ununited conquests burdens the commonwealth and often brings wounds from enemies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncoordinated expansions are often a liability, costing more to keep than they provide, and can leave the state vulnerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize dissolution after decisive military defeat
rubrics_metrics.description: If in war the enemies gain a final victory and the commonwealth's forces cannot keep the field, the commonwealth is dissolved and subjects are at liberty to protect themselves by any means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign (public soul) expiring leaves members unbound; though the sovereign's right cannot be extinguished by act of another, obligation of subjects may end when protection ceases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary office of sovereign: procuration of the people's safety and contentments
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign's office consists in procuring the safety of the people, not merely preservation but also lawful contentments of life that subjects may acquire without danger to the commonwealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation arises from the law of nature and accountability to God; the sovereign must ensure both protection and conditions for lawful industry and enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public instruction and laws rather than individual care
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign's care should be a general providence: public instruction (doctrine and example) and making and executing good laws so individuals can apply them to private cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction and laws are the conduit for protecting persons; sovereigns should not micromanage individuals beyond protecting from injuries and providing general frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not relinquish essential sovereign rights
rubrics_metrics.description: It is against sovereign duty to transfer or lay aside any essential rights of sovereignty (listed earlier): supreme judicature, making war and peace, judging necessities, levying money and soldiers, making officers, appointing teachers, and judging doctrines for public defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relinquishing means deserting means necessary to ends—if sovereign acknowledges himself subject to civil laws or renounces these powers the commonwealth is at risk of dissolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach people the grounds of sovereign rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign should not let people be ignorant or misinformed about the grounds and reasons of his essential rights; ignorance makes them easy to seduce to resist when those rights must be exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because such rights cannot be maintained by mere civil law or terror (which subjects may see as hostility), moral and rational instruction is required to instill natural-law obligations not to violate faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refute objections that there are no principles of reason for absolute sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections claiming no rational grounds exist for absolute sovereignty are mistaken; principles can be discovered by industry and time, analogous to how building art arose later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not yet discovered in practice, principles may be derived from reason and scripture; lack of historical recognition does not imply absence of reasoned grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter the objection of vulgar incapacity to understand sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that common people cannot understand these principles is weak—the real obstruction is interest: the powerful dislike doctrines that bridle their affections and the learned dislike ones exposing their errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common people, left untainted by elites' interests, can learn from public authority; the sovereign has a duty (and benefit) to cause them to be instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach citizens not to desire change of government or admire foreign forms
rubrics_metrics.description: People should be taught not to love other nations' forms of government more than their own; prosperity comes from obedience and concord, not the mere form (monarchy, aristocracy, or democracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desire for change often destroys commonwealths; reform by disobedience can destroy rather than renew the state (fable of daughters of Peleus). Obedience and concord are the sources of prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruct subjects not to adhere to popular men against the sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: People should not be led to admire or obey high-standing fellow subjects or assemblies (except the sovereign assembly) so as to defer obedience or honour proper to the sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influence must only be what is conveyed by sovereign authority; allowing popular men to seduce loyalty undermines sovereign power and unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach against speaking ill of or disputing sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a fault to speak evil of the sovereign representative or to argue and dispute his power, since such irreverence brings sovereign into contempt and slackens obedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This slackening of obedience endangers the commonwealth's safety; instruction should foster reverence and discourage public disparagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside times/days for instruction and law-reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Because people cannot be taught or retain instruction without dedicated time, certain times should be determined for assembly to hear duties and positive laws read and expounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Jewish Sabbath where law was read and people reminded of God's kingship; weekly or periodic public instruction reinforces knowledge of sovereign authority and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honour parents as part of public instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should be obedient to parents during tutelage and afterward show external signs of honour; fathers were originally sovereigns and parental honour aligns with civic duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching honour of parents supports social order and agrees with the fifth commandment; sovereigns should ensure such instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach justice as abstaining from depriving neighbours
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign ought to cause justice to be taught: taking from no man what is his, abstaining from violence, violation of conjugal honour, rapine, and fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show evils of false judgment, corrupted judges or witnesses which destroy propriety and justice; offences against private persons require consent or reasonable satisfaction to be pardoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inculcate sincerity of heart: intentions as injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: People must be taught that unjust intentions and designs (even when thwarted) are injustice as much as unjust acts; the pravity of will matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with the tenth commandment and the sum of the Second Table: mutual charity and love thy neighbour as thyself—morally internalized obligations, not merely external compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use universities to instruct youth correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities and schools are key conduits for instilling doctrines; instruction of the people depends on right teaching of youth at universities and law schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If universities propagate false doctrines (e.g., papal power over commonwealth), the sovereign must address that; historically universities upheld papal over civil power—thus they need proper guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administer justice equally to all ranks
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice must be equally administered to rich and poor so that great persons have no greater hope of impunity; inequality breeds insolence, hatred, and attempts to overthrow oppressing greatness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity consists in equal redress; offences against private persons cannot be pardoned without the injured party's consent; sovereign is subject to natural law like any subject in administering equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose equal taxation based on equal debt to the commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Equality of tax imposition depends on equality of the debt each owes for defence, not equality of riches; taxes should be proportionate to consumption/use rather than mere wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes seen as wages for those who hold the public sword; levying on consumed things charges people equally for the protection they receive and avoids defrauding the commonwealth by private luxury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public support for the truly unable (publique charity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who by unavoidable accident cannot maintain themselves should be provided for by the laws of the commonwealth rather than left to private charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is uncharitable for a sovereign to expose the impotent to uncertain private charity; public provision upholds social stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent idleness and encourage useful arts
rubrics_metrics.description: Able-bodied poor should be compelled to work; laws should encourage navigation, agriculture, fishing, and manufactures; transplant surplus population to less inhabited countries if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the world is overcharged, last remedy is war (provides subsistence by victory or death); better to structure society to avoid idle poor becoming a threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good laws must be necessary and perspicuous
rubrics_metrics.description: A good law is that which is needful for the good of the people and perspicuous: necessary (not a trap for money) and clear in causes/motives explaining why it was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws should direct to avoid harm from rash desires; unnecessary laws are traps or superfluous. Perspicuity comes from a declaration of causes: shorter, proper, and significant terms reduce ambiguity and unnecessary processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply punishments and rewards to the public benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Punishments should correct offenders or deter others; severest punishments reserved for crimes of most danger to the public (malice to government, contempt of justice, provoking public indignation); lenity for crimes of infirmity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punish leaders and teachers of commotion, not just the seduced poor. Rewards should recompense faithful service at minimal public expense and encourage service—do not buy peace by rewarding ambitious troublemakers as that breeds more mischief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose counsellors wisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereign must choose good counsellors—those most able and least likely to benefit by giving evil counsel and most knowledgeable of what conduces to peace and defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detecting who expects benefit from public troubles is hard; signs include soothing the people in unreasonable grievances by men whose estates cannot meet their expenses. Prefer advisers with knowledge and no incentive to create trouble.
